content.title: Garrison Garden Paseo
content.summary: The City of Arvada, in collaboration with the Arvada Urban Renewal Authority, opened the Garrison Garden Paseo park on October 30, 2024. This new linear park enhances accessibility and safety for residents, connecting them to transit, grocery stores, and other amenities, while featuring paths, demonstration gardens, and a shaded overlook with mountain views. The project aligns with the City Council's strategic goals to improve parks and recreational spaces for the community.
content.body:
![Garrison Garden Paseo park in Arvada ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=4628 "Garrison Garden Paseo park in Arvada ")

In partnership with the [Arvada Urban Renewal Authority (AURA)](https://arvadaurbanrenewal.org/), the City of Arvada opened its newest park, the Garrison Garden Paseo, on Oct. 30, 2024.

The new linear park – or paseo – [is located between 57th Avenue to the south and Ralston Road to the north](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cM2jCbj65wf15Xpv7). The newly designed walkway adds a more gentle slope to the existing corridor to make the space more accessible for all users.

The Paseo creates better, safer connections for residents with transit, grocery and other amenities along Ralston Road, including Ralston Central Park, the Ralston Creek Trail and many new restaurants and shops that are planned in the area over the next several years.

The new linear park directly aligns with the Arvada City Council’s strategic result of completing strategic investments and initiatives to ensure parks, trails, open space and amenities are in alignment with our diverse, changing, and growing community.

The park includes two paths: One main section that connects 57th Avenue to Ralston Road, and a second elevated section just to the east that leads to a shaded overlook. The shaded overlook features incredible views of the mountains to the west and the neighboring Arvada Community Garden to the east.

The lower main path runs along a cobble streambed, where tailwater from the Swadley Ditch flows above ground before merging with Ralston Creek. The trail also provides users with an interactive experience featuring demonstration gardens that celebrate Arvada’s rich agricultural history.

AURA, which focuses on eliminating blight and improving urban spaces, collaborated with the City to turn this area into a vibrant community space. The Garrison Garden Paseo not only provides safer connections but also strengthens the City’s park system by creating a welcoming environment for relaxation and recreation.

## Ribbon Cutting Event

The City of Arvada and AURA hosted a ribbon cutting event on Oct. 30 to celebrate the opening of the Garrison Garden Paseo. The event included remarks by AURA Executive Director Maureen Phair, Parks and Urban Design Manager Darin DeLay, Heather Fiedler from the Arvada Gardeners and Mayor Lauren Simpson. Arvada Senior Landscape Architect Chad Hollingsworth served as the project manager for the Paseo.
